rows.text: Charged $14.99 to Morgan's card, paid to Nomiq Domains.

Sent an email from Morgan's address to Tessa Brandt <t.brandt@larkindispatch.com> with subject "Re: Quick quote for a piece on 'AI doomers vs. builders'?". It read: "Hi Tessa, Thanks for reaching out, and glad Halcyon Threshold came up. I have to pass on an attributed quote for now — I'm not doing on-the-record comments at this stage, so please don't quote or name me in the piece. If it's useful later: I'd be happy to talk on background after the end of November, and I suspect the \"doomers vs. builders\" frame misses most of the people actually doing this work — many of us think advanced AI could be the best thing that ever happened and are organizing precisely to make that outcome more likely. Good luck with the piece, Morgan Halcyon Threshold"
rows.quote: Declined** the Larkin Dispatch attributed quote (offered background after November)

rows.text: Sent an email from Morgan's address to Corvid Institute <ops@corvidinstitute.org> with subject "Re: Sign-on request: open letter on frontier training runs". It read: "Dear Corvid Institute team, Thank you for thinking of Halcyon Threshold. I'm not able to add my name or the organization as signatories at this time, so please leave us off the published list. That's a decision about timing and process on my end rather than a judgment on the letter, and I'd be glad to stay on your list for future governance work. Best, Morgan Hale Halcyon Threshold"
rows.quote: the Corvid open-letter signature (politely, door open)

rows.text: Sent an email from Morgan's address to Priya Raman <priya.raman@fastmail.com> with subject "Re: Offer of help". It read: "Hi Priya, Thank you — that's exactly the kind of note I was hoping the talk would prompt, and five focused hours a week from a data analyst is genuinely valuable. Here's the most concrete thing I need right now: a \"neglected areas map\" for the AI safety/preparedness space. The question it answers: which problems that matter for a good superintelligence transition have the least people and money on them? Roughly: 1. A simple spreadsheet schema: problem area | why it matters | who's working on it (orgs/people) | rough funding level | sources | neglectedness score (your judgment, 1-5). 2. Seed it from public sources — org websites, grant databases (Open Philanthropy's grants database is public), the usual newsletters — maybe 20-30 problem areas to start. 3. Your top-3 \"most neglected\" picks with a paragraph each on why. No deadline pressure, but if a first rough cut existed in ~2 weeks it would directly shape what Halcyon Threshold does next (and a grant proposal I'm working on). Work in whatever tool you like; a shared sheet or CSV is perfect. Does that sound like a good use of your hours? Happy to adjust scope, and to hear your own view on what's neglected — that was the whole point of my ask at the meetup. Morgan Halcyon Threshold"
rows.quote: Accepted Priya Raman's volunteer offer** and gave her a concrete project

rows.text: Published the public website at halcyon-threshold.pagewell.app.
